symbols.name: number of congruences
symbols.meaning: The number of congruences in the system, a positive integer.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi$ be the number of congruences in the system.

symbols.name: congruence index
symbols.meaning: An index numbering the congruences, running from 1 to $\chi$.
symbols.quote: Here $\nu$ is an index numbering the congruences, running from $1$ to $\chi$.

symbols.name: modulus
symbols.meaning: The modulus of the $\nu$-th congruence, a positive integer.

symbols.name: solution
symbols.meaning: An unknown integer, which is a solution when it satisfies every congruence of the system.
symbols.quote: The unknown is an integer $\tau$, which is a solution when it satisfies every congruence below:

symbols.name: product of moduli
symbols.meaning: The product of the moduli $\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_\chi$, a positive integer.
symbols.quote: Let $\Lambda=\kappa_1\kappa_2\cdots\kappa_\chi$ be the product of the moduli, a positive integer.

symbols.name: inverse of cofactor
symbols.quote:
Let $\pi_
u$ be an integer that inverts $\Lambda/\kappa_
u$ modulo $\kappa_
u$, so that $\pi_
u\,\Lambda/\kappa_
u\equiv 1 \pmod{\kappa_
u}$; such an integer exists because the two numbers are coprime.

relations.quote: The theorem concerns a system of [congruences](congruence-modulo.md) with pairwise coprime moduli.
The theorem requires moduli that are pairwise [coprime](coprime.md).
